utterances.text: And pretty much would it be fair to say that it, more or less in general terms, sets out what you've already told us actually was implemented through your commander, Pandurevic? In other words, this kind of gives him some general guidance, and then in the end, on the attack on Srebrenica, he more or less complies with this particular task that was assigned to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is calling for speculation from this witness. He has already testified he's not sure he saw this. He wasn't at the attack on Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll lay some foundation with the next order, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Further down on page 4, do you see a section that deals with the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it in that section, it sets out what the Bratunac Brigade's functions or tasks are supposed to be in this campaign against Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is stated very clearly here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, based on your military experience and your background and your familiarity of reading orders such as this one, are you able to give us a general opinion as to how active the Bratunac Brigade was supposed -- was envisioned to be based on this section of the order of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at this document, Mr. Karnavas, I believe that the corps commander, when he put this together, he probably planned for the Bratunac Brigade not to be included in those forces that would be in the first lines of attack; but rather, that in the first line of the attack, there would be the Zvornik Brigade Battalion, as it says here, the battalion of the 2nd Romanija Brigade, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I could show you what has been marked as D42 for identification purposes, if you could look at it --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I won't be needing the map any longer, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to look at it, Mr. Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unlike the one before, I believe I saw this document at the time when it was written, on the 2nd or perhaps on the 3rd of July, 1995, most probably at the latest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, it's dated 2nd July, 1995, is it not?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I believe this was drafted early -- later in the evening or perhaps even at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please identify or describe to us what exactly is this document that has been marked for identification purposes as D42?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, as you can see in the header, it's a document by the Zvornik Brigade command dated 2nd of July, and it says: "Preparation order, establishment of a tactical group of the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade for carrying out combat operations in the Drina Corps zone." So this is a preparation order, in answer to your question, on the establishment of a tactical group for carrying out active combat operations in the Drina Corps zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now having looked at this document and having looked at the previous document which was marked for identification purposes as D16, and in particular, paragraph number 5 which denotes the tasks assigned to the Zvornik Brigade, would it be correct to state that the Zvornik Brigade order that we have here, more or less in general terms, fulfills the tasks that were assigned to it, at least on paper, as far as what the Zvornik Brigade would be involved in or be engaged in during the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, in the previous document entitled "Krivaja 1995," it speaks about the tasks of the battalion of the Zvornik Brigade and the directions of its attack. So that's one thing. Whereas here, you have the commander of the Zvornik Brigade establishing a unit, his unit. So these are not exactly related. On the one hand, here, you have the commander establishing a unit to perform tasks on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the unit was being formed to perform the tasks that it was assigned to it by the Drina Corps. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And would it not be fair to state that these units that were formed by -- was it Colonel or Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic? I want to make sure I get it -- I know he's a general now.

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a lieutenant-colonel, as it says. He was a lieutenant-colonel. I was, myself, a major.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, so and during the operation, Lieutenant-Colonel Vinko Pandurevic played a major role, did he not, along with these units he had formed?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you could look at what has been marked as D17 for identification purposes, most likely you have not seen this document. But if you could look at it, and it's an order for active combat actions drafted by the commander of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade on 5 July, 1995. If you could look at that.

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're quite right, I've never seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If I were to give you a few moments to look at it, might you be able to inform us whether this order drafted by Colonel Blagojevic comports with or is consistent with the tasks assigned to the Bratunac Brigade, pursuant to the Drina Corps' order of 2 July, 1995? Do you think you might be able to do that?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, by just going through this combat order very quickly, an order signed by Colonel Blagojevic and dated 5th of July, 1995, it appears to be in the same spirit as that given by the corps commander. It enumerates tasks for all four of the infantry battalions, the logistics units. Without looking further, three battalions on the whole should offer -- should give fire support from their own positions, but the 4th Battalion should carry out the main defence. Those were, generally speaking, the tasks given to them as we said before without going into further detail at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. But by just looking at it, it would be fair to say, would it not, that the Bratunac Brigade was given a much lesser role to play than, say, Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic in the attack on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, it's very difficult to form an assessment like that, an assessment of quite specific military issues. I'll try to make this as clear as I can. The whole of the Bratunac Brigade was there. It was their zone of combat activity. They had four of their battalions there. In terms of combat strength, they may not quite have been the same units as those brought in by Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic. But if I understand the corps commander's orders clearly, part of the units, or rather the 28th Division was to be blocked from the north while the attack was being carried out from the units positioned in the south, from Zelani Jadar, and that's precisely what it says here. Now, who was more important and who was less important, it's really very difficult for me to say, and I'm not sure who would be well positioned to make this assessment at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now the Bratunac Brigade had been located there for quite some time, as the Zvornik Brigade had, in its zone of operation or zone of defence?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be a hundred per cent certain, Mr. Karnavas, but I think that since the establishment of the Srebrenica enclave, if I remember correctly, maybe in the second half of April 1993, those units were more or less in the same place. As I said before, the 4th, or rather our former 8th Battalion which later became the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade, was resubordinated to them in very rough terms in the summer of 1994, and that's where those units were. Those units stayed there for a longer period of time. You're right in claiming that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I could focus your attention on July 12th, 1995, as I understand it on the morning of the 12th at approximately 6.00 in the morning or so, you received some information with respect to the location of the 28th Division, or at least parts of it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, that can be confirmed, or at least it seems to be -- we seem to have some evidence as a result of a conversation, an intercepted conversation with Radika Petrovic on the morning of July 12th, 1995, at approximately 6.08 hours. That would be 6.00 in the morning -- 8 minutes after 6.00 a.m. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean whether I talked to Radika?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, no, you received that information sometime around that period.

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, slight later perhaps. I did call Radika on the phone, but he wasn't in. He was somewhere at the position with his units, and I spoke to someone else, someone who may have been the duty officer at that headquarters. I think it was a bit later, not at 6.00. The first information I got, I checked with the units at the forward end towards the 2nd Corps. It was only after that that I tried to run this past Radika.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And the information that you were getting, was it solid intelligence information, or was the situation rather uncertain?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I believed this to be reliable information. However, events would later prove that that information was quite wrong, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In other words, you were not told the exact strength or the exact numbers of the 28th Division. Is that what you're referring to when you say that the information was wrong?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am referring to that, too, but just as illustration, later in the evening on the 12th, I had the information with me, and I went to where the ambush was. And the first information was that there were about 150 Muslim soldiers. And then later on, we got information that there were about 300. That's the information I had when I went into combat. And this information was later to prove totally wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know if you were receiving any information from the Bratunac Brigade, say, from the head of the -- the chief of the security and intelligence organ, Momir Nikolic? Was he providing any information to your intelligence folks over there?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I didn't receive this information personally. I took for granted what they told me at the 4th Battalion. I can't rule out the possibility that Captain Vukotic was exchanging intelligence with Nikolic, or perhaps Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric or even someone from the main staff. This may have been the case. I really don't know. I didn't personally get this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But the 28th Division, from where it had left and where it was heading would have to go through at least parts of -- between the Bratunac Brigade and the Milici Brigade. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're completely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then finally they would end up in your area, right around where the Zvornik Brigade would be located, before they could go to any number of directions to get to where the 2nd Corps was. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they entered the zone of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade by crossing the River Drina and entering the village of Glodi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to show you a couple -- I want to show you a daily combat report dated 12 July, 1995. It's from the 1st Light Infantry Bratunac Brigade. And if you could look at it, and it's marked for identification purposes as D44.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And also, if you could hand Mr. Obrenovic, D55, what has been marked as D55 for identification purposes, which is an urgent request from Colonel Blagojevic to the command of the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could look at those two documents, Mr. Obrenovic, take your time, I have a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: D44/1, this 12 July daily combat report, was P105.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It was not yet tendered, so I don't know how you best want to use the numbers. I just wanted to clarify the record of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I'm sorry to interrupt, to clarify the record, you mentioned Exhibit D55. In fact, it should be D45/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 45, I'm sorry. D44 and D45.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have taken a look at these documents, Mr. Karnavas. I hadn't seen them at the time, but I think that I was given them by my lawyers, they having received it from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, D44, what has been marked for identification purposes as D44, is a daily combat report from the Bratunac Brigade, and that's to the command of the Drina Corps, is it not?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can read that from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, from reading this document, one does not get a sense that there are any problems looming ahead, at least not for the Bratunac Brigade, and certainly there's nothing in here to suggest that there are any concerns with respect to where the 28th Division may be.

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're quite right. They don't mention that here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if I understand it correctly, the daily reports are compiled in the early afternoon. And I think by 4.00 or 5.00, they have to be sent to the Drina Corps. Is that correct? Or the corps command?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as I understand it, if the commander isn't there, or he's busy, the report is nonetheless prepared and sent off. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then the daily -- the Drina Corps would gather all of these various combat reports, and then prepare its own report that it would send to the main staff, and I think we looked at one of those today here. Am I correct on that?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we could look at what has been marked as D45 for identification purposes, and it says -- you'll see it's dated 12 July, 1995, same date as the daily combat report. We don't know exactly when it was sent off, or at least I can't tell. But we know that it says "urgent." Now, from reading that, what conclusion can you draw?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, from what I can read, this is a document of the 1st Light Bratunac Brigade written on the 12th of July. It says urgent, addressed to the command of the Milici Brigade, which means their neighbour on their right. And it is asking for information as to where the Milici forces are deployed on the left flank in relation to the Bratunac Brigade, and they mean that the passage between us, the gap, in order to close off that location. As it says here, the "Poturice," a derogatory term for Muslims, but actually the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And I do have two versions of this, and it's handwritten that it was sent actually on 13 July at 15 minutes past midnight. Right?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So it would appear that the Bratunac Brigade, at least, was unsure at this point in time as to where the 28th Division was and was asking for information from its neighbour as it should under these circumstances.

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they're asking their neighbours here to tell them where the forces of the neighbours are, that is, the left flank battalion of the Milici Brigade, so that they can organise a joint operation. And quite obviously, they don't have a clear idea of where the 28th Division is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. So they -- so Colonel Blagojevic wants to know what his neighbour is doing, where he's located, and that's the reason for this particular urgent message?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And would it not also appear that there seems to be a lack of good intelligence information as far as the 28th Division, based on this?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would seem so, and I've already said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if I could show you what has been marked as D46 for identification purposes, and it's an intelligence report from the intelligence organ of the Zvornik Brigade. Would you please look at that for a second. You probably have seen it already. Now, having looked at this intelligence report, it would appear that it's coming from the Zvornik Brigade. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document written by the assistant chief of staff for intelligence, Captain First Class Dusko Vukotic. I don't think this is his handwriting, actually, but he did sign it personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now at the top it's dated 12 July, 1995, but I see at the bottom, there's another date which is actually July 13th. And we have 1.10 under that, well, 1.10. Right. So that would be --

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, from this intelligence report, what -- can you give us a synopsis, just a -- what exactly this report tells us?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you expect me to read it out or to comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no, just to comment. Let me just tell you what I think, because I'm not used to reading these documents. But it would appear to me that the Zvornik Brigade just says, "we have seen from the Bratunac Brigade," they are also a little uncertain as far as what the situation is like. And then I look at the last sentence, and it says: "I estimate that the defence line from Baljkovice on the right to Ravno Brdo," and I'm killing the names, "on the left is threatened, on the primary axis of movement."

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you read this, what does this say?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you read this, Mr. Karnavas, that is to say, the whole report, then it just confirms the confusion of intelligence data that there was at the time. And at several points it gives us the frequencies, which means that the information he has at his disposal is coming in from intercept groups, and it's difficult to locate the places, the locations of the units that are being tapped into. It's just guesswork. And finally, it is his assessment that due to all these circumstances, the left flank has been threatened, the left flank of the Zvornik Brigade in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I understand -- I understand it that it is your belief that Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic may have been spending the night, that particular night and perhaps the previous night, that is, the 11th and the 12th, in the Zvornik area.

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I believe that might even be the case on the 13th, and you make that assessment based on a log, a fuel log, for his car. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic early on the morning of the 12th. We had a short conversation in the Zvornik Brigade headquarters, but yes, there is grounds for thinking along your lines. But on the morning of the 12th, we did have a conversation at the HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the day of the 12th after that conversation, did you by any chance contact your commander to inform him of the situation?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, Mr. Karnavas. We talked orally on the morning of the 12th and didn't hear from each other later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, is that because you had made a mental assessment that perhaps the situation was not quite as threatening as it appeared two or three days later? Might that be the case, or was there some other reason?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning, that was the reason. Later on, I didn't really have any physical possibility of doing that. I was in the field, on the ground, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, on the 13th, the day of the 13th, did you have more information during that particular day that would lead you to believe that perhaps the situation was unstable on the ground, for the Zvornik Brigade, that is?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, on the 13th during the morning, I was on the ground, and we did have information from the intercept groups that there were large forces in the depth of our territory. But through radio, we received information from General Zivanovic or the Drina Corps command that the road had been blocked, the Kasaba/Konjevic Polje Road, of course, and in fact that only small groups had managed to cross over, no large forces. So that for the time being, I personally thought that the corps command was in control of the situation more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Had you contacted on that particular day your commander, Pandurevic, to at least give him an update on the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Late in the evening, I talked to General Zivanovic, but I didn't talk to Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll get to that evening. During that day, did you by any chance contact Colonel Blagojevic of the Bratunac Brigade or the commander of the Milici Brigade to find out what information they may have for you?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I think the logistics officer from the Bratunac Brigade called me that evening about a tank. That was all. That was all the contact that I had personally with the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But at some point that evening, you did have a conversation with General Zivanovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you initiate that conversation, or did he call you?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I initiated the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it you were reaching out to General Zivanovic because at the time you believed he was still the commander of the Drina Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did General Zivanovic at that point indicate to you that he was no longer the commander and that perhaps you should consult with somebody else?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't point that out. I told him about an enormous column. He ordered me what to do, and I got on with it. But he didn't tell me anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Might I ask, was there a particular reason why you didn't reach out and try to locate your commander to inform him? Is there a particular reason why you went to Zivanovic, which is all the way up, bypassing Pandurevic, albeit you were, I believe by your own testimony, the acting commander at the time?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, the reason was that I estimated that those were enormous forces, and we had to step in urgently. That was my reasoning. There was no time to lose looking for Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic, wherever he was. My estimate was that this was the most intelligent thing to be done at the time, and that's why I did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, was this conversation before or after the conversation that you had with Drago Nikolic, your security, chief of security?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, Drago Nikolic called me, and then a bit later I called General Zivanovic. So after my conversation with the security officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll talk about that in a little bit. But first, I wanted to show you a couple of orders and see if we can get your assessment of this. And I'm referring to, for identification purposes, it's D28/1. And this is a Drina Corps order dated the 13th of July. And it's directed to the Bratunac/Milici/Skelani Brigades. And then at the same time, since we're dealing with this matter, perhaps you could also be furnished with D18 for identification purposes, which is an order that was drafted by the commander of the Bratunac Brigade dated 14th July, 1995. If you could please look at the corps order first, and then the order drafted by Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm ready, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Obrenovic. Now, the order dated 13 July, 1995, which is D28 for identification purposes, is this not an order from the Drina Corps to various brigades?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. This is an order from the command of the Drina Corps dated 13th of July, 1995, sent, as you said, to the Bratunac Light Brigade, Milici Light Brigade, and the Independent Battalion of Skelani, those three units. If one looks at the stamp, you can tell that the code was date, or rather hours, 2000 I believe, but this is a rather poor copy. It's difficult to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. It's 2000 or 2030, so that would make it late in the evening on the 13th. Now, this order, is it not an order for searching the terrain?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And is this not a normal military function after a battle, to search a particular terrain, especially if civilian population is expected to be moving through that terrain?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is obviously the decision of the commander of the Drina Corps for these forces or for most of these forces to be engaged on that task. That was his assessment and his decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. But I guess what I want to get at it is: The searching of terrain is a natural military operation after a battle such as the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is only to be expected, that this would have been an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so this order is being given to the Bratunac, the Milici, and the Skelani Brigade pretty much at the same time while you are in Zvornik contacting General Zivanovic, more or less alerting him to a threat that is headed your way, that is, the 28th Division. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct. It's quite obvious that this was roughly at the same time, a little bit before or a little bit later perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Can we draw any conclusions that perhaps the Drina Corps was also unaware of where the 28th Division was, its size, its threat, or potential threat, particularly to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be my conclusion. On the 13th around noon, or rather in the afternoon, we received information specifically from the corps command, from General Zivanovic, that the road had been blocked, and that there were no major forces moving in depth. And yet, on the 13th in the evening, we did see those, so you are entirely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And you don't have to be a genius to know that the 28th Division had a couple of options to start with. They could head towards Zepa, which was really not an option, or they would head towards Tuzla. And so you really don't have to be a military trained officer to know that they're probably going to go towards Tuzla because that's the only realistic available option left for them. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right, Mr. Karnavas. On the 12th, we even received an order from the command of the Drina Corps to prevent a breakthrough, I think that was the wording, by the 28th Division. The prediction was that this would include Tuzla, Kladanj, and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if I could get you to look at what has been marked as D18 for identification purposes. And this is an order prepared by Colonel Blagojevic with respect to ground search. Take a quick look at it, and then after you've skimmed it, if you could focus on paragraph number 4. Just read that thoroughly and carefully, please.

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 4 of this order from the 1st Bratunac Brigade says: "From its positions, the 4th Infantry Battalion will control the area in front of it, spreading from Lupoglav to Ravni Buljim, and reaching forward as far as Mratinsko Brdo and Sandici."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. First, let's talk about this document. Does this document not appear to be an implementing order at brigade level of the Drina Corps order dated the previous day signed by General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you look at the header, you can see that Colonel Blagojevic refers to that very same order by the Drina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And does it not, in looking at this order, when you look at paragraphs number 1, 2, and 3, he sets out in coordinates what portions of the terrain the 1st, the 2nd, and the 3rd Battalion will be searching?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it appears.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take it if we had the time, or if it were relevant, I could show you a map, and you would be able to plot it out and figure out exactly which area each battalion was tasked to search?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I could find these on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when you get to the 4th Battalion, it would appear, would it not, that they're not really being asked to do any searching?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that they should stay in their positions and control the area as ordered by firing from where they were. That's my reading of the document, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But when we say "control," in military terms, is he not asking the 4th Battalion to maintain their defensive positions which, in fact, they held for a year or two years earlier, maybe even three years?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you look at this order from the -- from Colonel Blagojevic, which is dated the 14th, would it also not appear based on what he's tasking the 4th Battalion, that perhaps at the Bratunac Brigade level, at the command level there, there seems to be a lack of correct information with respect to the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: Dragan Obrenovic [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think I'm right on the dot, Your Honour. I could go on, but I'm sure folks want to go home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 7th day of October, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.31 p.m.,
